$comment: Cloudflare spend-guard thresholds, the one source for agent/plans/PLAN-cloudflare-spend-guard.md. `notifications.products` is upserted by `PYTHONPATH=.ci python3 -m rediacc_ci.ops.cf_notifications` as one `spend-guard:<product>` billing_usage_alert policy each, emailed to WK_OPERATOR_EMAIL. A limit is in the product's base unit per billing cycle (requests, CPU ms, bytes, operations).

worker_requests.why: Workers requests, about twice the 10 million the Workers Paid plan includes. Configured beside worker_standard_request because the API accepts both and the billed line item is not documented.

worker_standard_request.why: Workers standard-usage-model requests, the same 20 million ceiling as worker_requests.

worker_standard_cpu_ms.why: Workers CPU time, about twice the 30 million ms Workers Paid includes.

r2_storage.why: R2 storage, 5 TB (decimal). Operator /ask 2026-10-30 "let's make it 5TB": hostinger backups (171 GB stored, 500 GB quota) took the account to 409 GB against the old 200 GB alert. Spend basis: at the R2 Standard rate of $0.015 per GB-month, a full 5 TB is about $75 a month, against about $2 a month for the retained release folders the old 200 GB figure was sized around.

r2_class_a_operations.why: R2 Class A (writes, lists), twice the 1 million included.

r2_class_b_operations.why: R2 Class B (reads), twice the 10 million included.

observability.wanted: Workers Observability ingestion 40 GB and storage 8 GB-month (80 percent of the included 50 GB and 10 GB-month)
observability.evidence: 2026-10-23: POST alerting/v3/policies with every candidate product name tried (worker_observability_events, worker_observability_ingestion, worker_observability_storage, worker_logs_events, observability_ingestion and nine more) answered `Error 17106: Invalid product selection.`; available_alerts lists no product values (AvailableValues null).
observability.fallback: The account-level billing_budget_alert `Default budget alert (auto-created)` (total_spend_dollars 10, emailed to the operator) covers it in dollars; the weekly cf_usage_report reads the volume; Dashboard > Notifications > Add > Usage Based Billing lists the product once Cloudflare offers it.

containers.wanted: Containers capped at the cost guard's 25 instances per target (max_instances in code), alarmed per application on vCPU-seconds and GiB-seconds
containers.evidence: 2026-10-23: containers, containers_vcpu, containers_memory, container_vcpu_seconds, container_memory_gib_seconds, cloudchamber_cpu_usage, cloudchamber_memory_usage, cloudchamber_disk_usage and eleven more answered `Error 17106: Invalid product selection.`
containers.fallback: The same 10 USD billing_budget_alert; check_proxy_cost_guard.py caps max_instances (25 per target, operator ruling ASKED:2026-10-26T15:26Z) and sleep_after in code, and the weekly cf_usage_report alarms on the containersMetricsAdaptiveGroups GraphQL dataset (see `report`).

existing_policies: Default budget alert (auto-created): billing_budget_alert, total_spend_dollars 10, created by Cloudflare 2026-07-21 for PayGo budget monitoring; not managed here

report_reason: r2_storage_bytes: 5 TB, operator /ask 2026-10-30 "let's make it 5TB" (the same value as notifications.r2_storage.limit). containers_*: per Containers application (one proxy target). Each per-metric ceiling alone is about 50 USD a month (20M GiB-seconds x 0.0000025 = 50 USD; 2.5M vCPU-seconds x 0.00002 = 50 USD), so the two together could reach 100 USD; containers_target_usd_month is the ~$50/target ruling in dollars, memory plus vCPU together, and bounds the pair; containers_total_usd_month is 7 targets x 50 USD = 350 USD. Operator ruling ASKED:2026-10-26T16:35Z, "Raise to ~$50/target".

worker_observability.sampling_ceiling_reason: operator ruling ASKED:2026-10-26T05:02Z 'Keep 1 everywhere': PLAN-cloudflare-spend-guard T4 measured total Worker telemetry at about 0.9% of the 50 GB allowance (c0b8fc69), so no Worker samples below 1; revisit if volume crosses 25%
